section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the superiority of serving G-d through mundane activities lies in it being analogous to repentance, revealing the soul's true will even amidst concealment.
section.t: And based on this, the advantage of the service of "in all your ways know Him" and "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven" will be understood
(not only regarding the effect on the world,
but rather)
also regarding the person
(the soul),

for that the soul, through its service in its descent below, becomes a "baal teshuvah" (master of return/repentance), is primarily through the service of doing permissible things for the sake of Heaven154.
And the explanation is,
behold it is written155
"And your people are all righteous,"
and the reason for this is that the true essence of each and every Jew is
(as above in section 12)
his G-dly soul.
And as the ruling of the Rambam
(cited above there)
that the true will of each and every Jew is to do everything that is the will of G-d,
and when one coerces him
(and certainly when he himself coerces himself)
to do some mitzvah,
his evil inclination is weakened and his true will is revealed in him.
And since at that moment when he is engaged in Torah and mitzvos his true will of the G-dly soul is revealed in him,
behold at that moment he is in the category of a tzaddik (righteous person).
For although even at that very moment there could be matters of the opposite of holiness in him,
nevertheless,
since the true reason that he fulfills the mitzvah is because his inner will has been revealed in him,
behold regarding the mitzvah he performs, he is in the category of a tzaddik.
[And this is what is meant that in the request "and give me bread to eat and a garment to wear" it is not mentioned that this will be in a manner of peace,
for the matter of peace applies when there is an opposing force
[and as the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace"156
(which relates to the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev157)
that this is from the aspect of
(as the verse continues156)
"from the battle against me"],
and therefore just as regarding a tzaddik it is not applicable to say that his service is in peace,
since he has no158
evil inclination at all,
so too is it regarding the Torah and mitzvos
(bread and garment)
of each Jew,
since at that moment he stands in the revelation of the will of the G-dly soul,
and the Torah and mitzvos he does are from the will of the soul,
the aspect of the tzaddik within him].
However, when he engages in permissible matters,
since his doing these matters is because they are the need of the body and its sustenance and vitality159
or also from his animal soul
(which naturally desires worldly matters160)
which conceal and hide his G-dly soul,
therefore,
that his engagement in permissible matters is for the sake of Heaven and in a manner of "know Him,"
is analogous to the service of teshuvah (repentance/return).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in exile, even the service of Torah and mitzvos requires the prior aspect of teshuvah to overcome obstacles, unlike in Temple times.
section.t: And now, more generally,
also the service of Torah and mitzvos when it is in a manner that a person must subdue his inclination,
and especially in the time of exile when there are many hindrances and obstacles to engaging in Torah and mitzvos and one must overcome them,
is included in the service of teshuvah.
And with this will be understood what is said in the Zohar161
that when Yaakov saw the poverty and suffering that would be in the time of the exile of Edom,
(and especially)
at the end of the time of exile,
he said "and I will return in peace to my father's house" and "and He will give me bread to eat and a garment to wear,"
and it is not understood,

behold in the verse it says "and He will give me bread etc." and afterwards "and I will return in peace etc." and why does the Zohar precede "and I will return in peace" before "and He will give me bread etc."162.
And the explanation can be said,
that since the Zohar there speaks about the matter of the poverty and suffering of the time of exile
[which is a third explanation regarding "and Yaakov went out... and he went to Charan,"
that this going out and going is
[not from the aspect of Binah to Malchus and also not from the aspect of Malchus to Biyah
(as per the two explanations brought above in section 3),
but rather]
to the time of exile163.
For this is also as our Sages said39
that Charan is the matter of the burning anger of the Place in the world,
that this matter is
(primarily)
in the time of exile],
therefore it precedes "and I will return in peace etc." before "and He will give me bread etc. and garment etc.,"
for from the aspect of the concealments and coverings of the time of exile,
even the service of Torah and mitzvos
(bread and garment)
is through the precedence of the matter of teshuvah
("and I will return in peace")
which includes
(as above)
the overcoming of hindrances and obstacles.
And in the verse it says "and He will give me bread etc. and garment etc." before "and I will return in peace etc.,"
for the matter of "and Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan" as it is in every generation
(even before the exile)
is the descent of the soul below
(in general,
and not the descent of exile),
and since in the time of the Temple the service of teshuvah is the refinement of permissible matters, while the service of Torah and mitzvos is
(generally)
the service of the tzaddikim,
therefore it says immediately "and He will give me bread to eat and a garment to wear,"
and it does not first precede "and I will return in peace."
And on the contrary,
"and He will give me bread etc." is before "and I will return in peace,"
for after the service of Torah and mitzvos which is appropriate for the G-dly soul,
then specifically can the refinement of permissible matters be
("and I will return in peace").
And in the manner of our Sages' saying164
"Adorn yourself first, and then adorn others."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the teshuvah of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven" is superior, as it reveals the G-dly soul within the body and animal soul itself.
section.t: And it can be said,
that the teshuvah of the service of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven" is more elevated than the teshuvah of fulfilling Torah and mitzvos in the time of exile,
and also than simple teshuvah for transgressions.
For the matter of the teshuvah of fulfilling Torah and mitzvos in the time of exile is
(as above in section 8)
that one overcomes the hindrances and obstacles of the exile and does not take them into account.
And similarly regarding simple teshuvah,
for the matter of teshuvah is that he leaves his previous state.
And in the language of the Rambam
(cited above in section 15)
"Yesterday he was separated from the L-rd G-d of Israel... and today he is attached to the Shechinah."
However, the teshuvah of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven,"
since that he engages in permissible matters
("your deeds")
is from his body and his animal soul
(as above),
and that he does them for the sake of Heaven,
even though this is from the aspect of the soul,
behold this is not that the soul overcomes the body and animal soul
(and leaves them),
but rather,
that in this very action which is from the body and animal soul, there is the intention of "for the sake of Heaven" which is from the soul.
And this matter
(the revelation of the G-dly soul within the matters of the body and animal soul itself)
is a greater novelty than that the soul overcomes the concealments and coverings and leaves them.
And since the superiority of teshuvah over the service of the tzaddikim is from the novelty within it
(as above in section 15),
it follows that the primary superiority of teshuvah is in the teshuvah of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven."
